newsitem.title: UK: LatAm Eurobond spreads tighten on Argentina bond.
newsitem.headline: LatAm Eurobond spreads tighten on Argentina bond.

text.p: Spreads on Latin American international bonds tightened on Wednesday following the successful launch of Argentina's jumbo bond, traders said.
"Spreads have come in by around 10 basis points in anticipation of Argentina's bond performing well," said an emerging market debt trader at a European bond.
On Tuesday, Argentina issued a $2.0 billion 20-year global bond which will be priced later to yield 462.5 basis points over U.S. Treasuries, below the 475 b.p. spread talk.
The deal was three times oversubscribed, Argentina's treasury secretary Pablo Guidotti said, and new investors such as insurance companies and mutual funds bought the paper.
A rise in cross-over buying -- when non-emerging market specialists buy emerging market debt -- is the driving force behind Argentina's success, dealers said.
"(Institutional) investors are keen to buy yield, and following recent spread tightening are extending duration to get the higher returns," said a syndicate manager at a U.S. bank.
"Improved fundamentals in Mexico and Argentina are also boosting their confidence," he said.

The European bank trader said: "There definitely is a trend there which is one reason why the 20-year Argentina deal is expected to perform better than any other deal. Cross-over buying is now stronger than it was for Mexico's recent deal."
Mexico launched a $1.0 billion 10-year global bond on January 9 at a 335 b.p. spread over U.S. Treasuries.
The deal tightened in to around 310 b.p. last week when Mexico prepaid outstanding loans to the U.S. Treasury and the International Monetary Fund. On Wednesday, the spread was quoted at 302 b.p.
